record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Do there exist chiral tessellations of spherical space-forms?

evidence.quote: Problem 13 Determine whether there exist chiral tessellations of spherical space-forms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A spherical space-form is a quotient manifold of the form $S^n/\Gamma$, where $S^n$ is the unit $n$-sphere (with $n \geq 2$) equipped with its standard round metric and $\Gamma$ is a finite group of isometries of $S^n$ acting freely on $S^n$.

An abstract polytope of rank $n+1$ is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$ with a strictly monotone rank function whose elements (called faces) have ranks in $\{-1, 0, 1, \dots, n+1\}$, satisfying: (i) there is a unique least face (rank $-1$) and a unique greatest face (rank $n+1$); (ii) every maximal chain (flag) has exactly $n+3$ elements; (iii) $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected; and (iv) the diamond condition holds, namely for any two faces $F<G$ with $\mathrm{rank}(G)-\mathrm{rank}(F)=2$ there are exactly two faces strictly between $F$ and $G$. A tessellation of a spherical space-form $S^n/\Gamma$ is a face-to-face decomposition of $S^n/\Gamma$ into closed convex spherical cells that realises geometrically an abstract polytope of rank $n+1$.

Two flags of $\mathcal{P}$ are $i$-adjacent if they differ exactly in their rank-$i$ face. The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ of an abstract polytope acts freely on flags. A polytope (or tessellation) is called regular if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts transitively on the flags, and chiral if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ has exactly two orbits on the flags such that adjacent flags lie in distinct orbits. Equivalently, a chiral tessellation has maximal rotational symmetry but no symmetry that reverses orientation/flag-orbit.

Question: Does there exist an integer $n \geq 2$, a finite fixed-point-free group $\Gamma$ of isometries of $S^n$, and a chiral tessellation of the spherical space-form $S^n/\Gamma$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search found extensive literature on chiral abstract polytopes and on symmetric (regular/chiral) tessellations of Euclidean space-forms (where it is known that only the n-torus admits chiral tessellations, and only for n=2), but no source confirming a resolution of the analogous question for spherical space-forms. The status of the existence of chiral tessellations of spherical space-forms appears not to be settled in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Symmetric Tessellations on Euclidean Space-Forms
status_evidence.snippet: For n ≥ 2, the n-torus is the only n-dimensional compact euclidean space-form which can admit a regular or chiral tessellation, and such a tessellation can only be chiral if n = 2.
status_evidence.claim: The analogous (Euclidean) problem has been resolved, but the spherical case is treated separately and not addressed by this Euclidean classification.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry of Polytopes and Polyhedra (Handbook chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of regular and chiral polytopes and tessellations; very little is known about classification of chiral polytopes by topological type.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys indicate that chiral polytope/tessellation classification in various ambient spaces remains incomplete.
